articleBody:
Tearing out an outdated or unused bathtub sounds straightforward, but jumping in without a clear checklist can leave you dealing with water leaks or unsealed framing. 

Use this checklist to ensure your bathroom project stays organized and safe:

- [ ] Shutoff valve check — Confirm that dedicated hot and cold shutoff valves operate smoothly without leaking before any tools touch the tub.
- [ ] Replacement fixture dimensions — Verify the exact rough-in measurements of your planned shower base or new fixture before disconnecting anything.
- [ ] Clear exit path measurement — Measure interior door frames, hallways, and stairwells to confirm the bulky tub can physically exit your home.
- [ ] Concealed moisture inspection plan — Prepare moisture-resistant replacement materials in case rot or mold is discovered behind wet-wall surfaces.
- [ ] Dedicated breaker verification — Confirm surrounding GFCI outlets and light switches near wet areas are identified and switched off before demolition.
- [ ] Waste and drain alignment — Check whether your new shower drain requires relocating the subfloor waste pipe to maintain proper gravity fall.
- [ ] Surface protection setup — Lay heavy-duty floor runners and dust barriers along access routes to protect adjoining flooring from heavy debris.
- [ ] Disposal logistics plan — Arrange safe transport and haul-away methods for heavy acrylic units or massive cast-iron fragments.

How to use this checklist:
Review every item before beginning demolition so your plumbing lines, framing, and surfaces stay intact.
